title: What Is Artificial Intelligence?
summary: How a machine can learn patterns from examples, and what it still cannot do.

steps.title: Learning from examples
sentences: Artificial intelligence, or AI, is computer software that can do tasks that usually need human thinking.
Most modern AI learns from many examples rather than following only fixed rules.
Show a program thousands of pictures of cats and dogs, and it learns the patterns that tell them apart.

steps.title: Where you meet it
sentences: AI helps your phone recognise a voice, suggests videos, translates between languages and helps doctors study scans.
It is also used in maps to find the fastest way home.
Chat programs can write text because they have learned patterns from a huge amount of writing.

steps.title: What it cannot do
sentences: AI does not understand the world like a person does.
It can make mistakes, repeat unfair patterns found in its data, or say something that sounds sure but is wrong.
So people must check its work, especially for health, news and school facts.

steps.title: You in charge
sentences: AI is a tool, and people decide how it is used.
Use it to learn, but do your own thinking and keep your own voice.
The best way to be ready for the future is to keep learning how to ask good questions.

facts: The term artificial intelligence was first used at a workshop at Dartmouth in 1956.
Modern AI needs large amounts of computing power and electricity.
A calculator is not usually called AI, because it follows fixed rules.

quiz.q: How do many modern AI programs learn?
quiz.why: They find patterns in lots of examples.

quiz.q: Which is true about AI answers?
quiz.why: AI can make mistakes, so check them.

quiz.q: Who decides how AI is used?
quiz.why: People build and choose how to use AI.

notes: AI is changing quickly; this lesson explains the stable ideas only.
